routes.description: Establish that naturalism has greater intrinsic probability and that physical reality, biological history, embodied mentality, suffering, moral handicaps, and nonresistant nonbelief are collectively more expected on naturalism than on theism.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds by defending the comparative-probability method, showing that the cited evidence supplies independent or cumulative support for naturalism, and answering theistic appeals to creation, fine-tuning, information, reason, morality, and science.

motionBridge.description: Connect naturalism's intrinsic plausibility and total comparative evidential fit to the conclusion that it better explains reality than theism.

centralBridges.description: Establish a defensible intrinsic-probability advantage for naturalism through modesty and coherence without assuming the evidential conclusion.
Show that physical reality, evolution, embodied minds, suffering, moral handicaps, and hiddenness have greater expectedness on naturalism.
Show that creation, fine-tuning, biological information, reason, morality, and scientific order do not yield a superior theistic explanation.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Distinguish causal naturalism from scientism and from denial of every abstract, acausal, or nonphysical reality.
Preserve comparative inference by addressing alternative hypotheses, evidential dependencies, and the limits of claims based on unresolved phenomena.

routes.description: Establish that a prior intelligent personal agent better accounts for cosmic creation and sustenance, fine-tuning, biological information, rational thought, objective morality, natural order, evil, and the foundations of science than naturalism does.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds by supporting the principal theistic inferences, showing that their explanatory domains form a cumulative case, and answering naturalistic objections from simplicity, evolution, embodied minds, suffering, hiddenness, and moral disagreement.

motionBridge.description: Connect the cumulative explanatory case for an intelligent personal ground to the conclusion that theism better explains reality than naturalism.

centralBridges.description: Establish that cosmic origin or contingency, fine-tuning, biological information, and natural directedness support an intelligent transcendent cause.
Establish that rational agency, logical and mathematical order, and objective moral obligation require grounding unavailable to naturalism.
Show that physical determination and exclusively natural causes leave material explanatory commitments unsupported or internally unstable.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Supply theistic accounts of suffering, nonresistant nonbelief, evolution, and moral disagreement sufficient to resist their proposed evidential force.
Explain how divine grounding and intelligent causation can complement scientific accounts of regular operation and inquiry.

sections.title: Worldview Scope, Intrinsic Probability, and Comparative Method
sections.rationale: The motion depends on how naturalism and theism are defined, how modesty and coherence affect prior probability, and how evidence and alternative explanations are combined without invalid inference.

sections.title: Cosmic Existence, Contingency, Order, and Fine-Tuning
sections.rationale: Physical reality, cosmic origin and sustenance, life-permitting conditions, and natural regularity form a principal clash over whether reality points to natural necessity or transcendent agency.

sections.title: Evolution, Biological Information, and Life's History
sections.rationale: Evolutionary evidence, fossil history, genetic information, and proposed natural origins of life test the competing expectations and explanatory resources of both worldviews.

sections.title: Embodied Mind, Rational Reliability, and Scientific Knowledge
sections.rationale: Mind-brain dependence, determinism, evolved cognition, logical and mathematical order, and the presuppositions of science bear directly on whether either worldview can account for reliable reasoning.

sections.title: Objective Morality, Suffering, and Moral Agency
sections.rationale: Moral grounding, pain, allegedly gratuitous evil, neurological moral handicaps, freedom, and moral disagreement jointly test each worldview's account of value and morally significant experience.

sections.title: Divine Hiddenness and Overall Explanatory Balance
sections.rationale: Nonresistant nonbelief and proposed reasons for divine silence create a direct relational test of theism, while the final cumulative comparison connects all evidential domains to the motion.

chunk-001:chunk-001-candidate-01.proposition: Naturalism has greater intrinsic probability than theism because it makes fewer assertions while remaining comparably coherent.

chunk-001:chunk-001-candidate-02.proposition: Physical reality favors naturalism because naturalism requires it, whereas theism permits God to create disembodied minds or nothing at all.

chunk-001:chunk-001-candidate-03.proposition: Biogeography, vestigial organs, natural selection, embryology, and fossils make biological evolution more expected on naturalism than on theism or special creationism.

chunk-001:chunk-001-candidate-04.proposition: The biological usefulness and morally random distribution of pain and pleasure are more expected under unguided natural processes than under a morally perfect creator.

chunk-001:chunk-001-candidate-05.proposition: The dependence of human mentality on physical brains favors naturalism over theism, which entails an unembodied divine mind and did not require embodied created minds.

chunk-001:chunk-001-candidate-06.proposition: Neurologically caused empathy deficits and moral handicaps are more expected on indifferent naturalism than on theism, where God creates morally impaired humans.

chunk-001:chunk-001-candidate-07.proposition: Nonresistant people who are open to relationship with God yet cannot believe are expected on indifferent naturalism but surprising given a perfectly loving God.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-02.proposition: The cumulative theistic case does not prevail merely by citing phenomena compatible with naturalism when positing God assumes rather than explains those phenomena.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-03.proposition: A life-permitting universe does not clearly favor theism when probabilities over possible universes are unknown and the universe's pervasive hostility to life fits naturalism better.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-07.proposition: Determinism and evolutionary origins do not by themselves undermine cognition because a mechanism's causal origin is distinct from its truth-tracking reliability and information transmission.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-09.proposition: Experimental support for an RNA-world pathway partially confirms that biological information may arise naturally, although the origin question remains unsettled.

chunk-004:c004-07.proposition: Naturalism gives physical reality explanatory priority over mental causal reality without entailing scientism, materialism, or denial of autonomous abstract and acausal realities.

chunk-001:chunk-001-candidate-08.proposition: The universe's beginning and fine-tuning point to a spaceless, timeless, immaterial, powerful, personal, and intelligent creator.

chunk-001:chunk-001-candidate-09.proposition: Naturalism undermines rational belief because physically determined thoughts would be reactions produced by nonrational causes rather than reasoned conclusions.

chunk-001:chunk-001-candidate-10.proposition: The ordered information in DNA is best explained by an intelligent mind because messages, programs, and codes arise from intelligent sources.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-08.proposition: Macroevolution neither explains genetic and structural information nor entails naturalism, since evolutionary processes could themselves operate under divine sustenance.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-09.proposition: The amount of pain does not disprove God because treating pain as objectively bad presupposes moral standards, while Christianity supplies restoration and ultimate justice.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-01.proposition: God may permit temporary honest nonbelief because delayed conversion can produce greater maturity, broader influence, or reduced culpability.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-02.proposition: Objective moral obligations depend on objective goodness, and objective goodness exists only if God exists.

chunk-004:c004-04.proposition: Contingent reality requires God as a continuously sustaining, noncontingent and fully actual cause, so creation would cease to exist without divine conservation.

chunk-004:c004-06.proposition: Science depends on prior philosophical commitments, and excluding intelligent causes before examining evidence is a philosophical restriction rather than a scientific conclusion.

chunk-005:chunk-005-candidate-01.proposition: Theism better explains creation, reason, information, morality, evil, and science than naturalism does.

chunk-005:chunk-005-candidate-06.proposition: Naturalistic probability arguments rely on purposive mathematical and logical laws that are grounded in a transcendent mind.
